versions.name: RXV2-0.9.647-ports
versions.notes: New Ports page (Rotorflight's Ports tab): each flight-controller UART gets one plain choice - nothing, receiver (CRSF, SBUS or IBUS), dongle on a wire (MSP 115200), ESC telemetry, S.Port telemetry, GPS or blackbox; other setups are kept as they are; one receiver port only; Save writes the ports and the receiver protocol, saves, restarts the flight controller and waits for it. With this, a new receiver never needs the configurator: the port is set from the phone over USB. Includes 0.9.646.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.646-remove-saves
versions.notes: In-flight adjustments: Remove asks 'Remove ... from the flight controller?' and saves straight away (Malcolm 2026-09-11: did not realise Save was still needed); any other edit turns the Save button orange with 'unsaved changes' until saved. Includes 0.9.645.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.645-cable-wording
versions.notes: The USB-only pages now say 'connect a USB cable between the flight controller's USB socket and the receiver's USB socket' (Malcolm, after the successful Goblin test with the transmitter on). Includes 0.9.644.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.644-save-retry
versions.notes: In-flight adjustments: Save retries any of its 43 writes that the receiver answers 'busy with a transmitter edit' or 'did not respond' to, so saving with the transmitter on no longer stops at the first collision with the transmitter's own Rotorflight traffic (Goblin bench, 2026-09-11 07:54). Includes 0.9.643.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.643-usb-tx-on
versions.notes: A receiver now adopts a flight controller on its USB socket even while the transmitter is on (the USB task does the opening, the radio loop never waits), so the USB pages work in the usual bench setup: transmitter on, blades off. The command line and the reboot-to-apply settings still wait for the transmitter to be off. Includes 0.9.642.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.642-usb-review2
versions.notes: Second pass from the review: an MSP request on a receiver without a CRSF line (SBUS/IBUS/PPM, or FC telemetry off) is dropped rather than sent as CRSF frames onto the servo line once the USB cable is out; the telemetry-setup repair writes only over the CRSF link; long command-line output (dump) keeps its tail so the prompt is always seen; a half-installed USB host is undone; the USB socket switch is refused on a dongle; the USB-only pages say when the transmitter is keeping the USB link from opening; Find a setting knows the USB socket switch. Includes 0.9.641.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.641-usb-review
versions.notes: From the adversarial review of the receiver USB host: the USB device is now opened and closed by the USB task, never by the main loop (a misbehaving device can no longer hold the radio loop); an unplug while the command line is open closes the command line instead of leaving MSP dead until a reboot; a re-plugged device gets fresh open attempts; a device that leaves before it is opened is dropped at once; the dongle no longer types MSP into an open command line either; the simulator and dongle pages show a refusal instead of pretending to reboot. Includes 0.9.640.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.640-usb-guards
versions.notes: Guards on top of 0.9.639 (receiver hosts the flight controller over USB): the command line and the reboot-to-apply settings (USB socket, simulator, dongle mode) are refused while the transmitter has been linked in the last 3 s; the USB device is opened or closed only after 3 s without a link; MSP is never typed into an open command line; the queue is emptied when a flight controller (re)connects; a bank hold is kept over USB on non-CRSF receivers; the flight controller's own 'armed' word refuses configuration on a receiver too; a gone USB device can no longer crash the board; 'msc' is refused on the command line; state.json gains fc_link (usb, crsf, uart or none). Home page says 'flight controller on USB' and warns while the command line is open. Includes 0.9.639.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.639-usb-on-receiver
versions.notes: A RECEIVER now hosts the flight controller on its USB socket exactly as the dongle does (Malcolm 2026-09-11: 'Yes let's do it'): a USB-C cable from the receiver to the flight controller gives the app every Rotorflight setting (the full adjustments read, In-flight adjustments, the Command line), while the CRSF line keeps carrying channels and telemetry. Automatic; Setup has a 'USB socket' switch to turn it off; simulator mode uses the socket instead. Flight rules: USB sends are queued to a task (the radio loop never waits), the device is opened or closed only with no transmitter linked, and an unplug falls back to the radio link at once. Includes 0.9.638.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.638-usb-wording
versions.notes: Help on In-flight adjustments and Command line: the USB cable runs from the dongle to the flight controller, not to a laptop (Malcolm: some might assume it needs the laptop). Includes 0.9.637.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.637-help-try
versions.notes: In-flight adjustments help (Malcolm): after the boxes fill with the current value, change one or two to the values you want to try and leave the first box as it is, so a flick of the switch takes you back. Includes 0.9.636.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.636-help
versions.notes: Help screens: the In-flight adjustments and Command line pages now have the ? button (they were the only pages without it) with short, step-ordered help - setting one up, Switch, Knob, Banks, Numbers, USB; commands, leaving, what is paused. Includes 0.9.635.
